# Private vulnerability reporting is off outside the engine

## Context

Found on 2026-11-15 while reviewing #21007, which adds the engine's `.github/SECURITY.md` (Resolves #21004). The policy's Scope section sends a finding in another repository to that repository's reporting channel, as #21004 prescribed. I wrote that sentence in #21004 without reading the other repositories' setting.

## The Problem

Read at 2026-11-15T21:43:46Z over the 46 public, non-archived repositories of the organisation (`gh repo list neomjs --visibility public --no-archived`): `gh api repos/neomjs/<repo>/private-vulnerability-reporting` answers `enabled: true` for `neo` and `false` for the other 45, among them `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-skills`, `neo-agent-institution`, `create-app`, `devindex` and `pages`. The community profile names no security policy for any of them (four return no profile), and the organisation has no public `.github` repository that would supply a default one.

A person who finds a vulnerability in the Brain's MCP servers has no private path: the engine's policy sends them to the Brain, and the Brain offers a public issue.

## The Architectural Reality

- Private vulnerability reporting is a repository setting. An organisation owner or security manager can switch it on for all public repositories at once, and a security configuration covers repositories created later ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-repository-security-advisories/configuring-private-vulnerability-reporting-for-an-organization)).
- The engine's policy text in #21007: "Report vulnerabilities in other repositories of the organization through those repositories' reporting channels." It becomes true the moment the setting is on.
- `Design authority: n/a — calls no existing behavior wrong.`

## The Fix

1. **The operator's step** (an organisation owner's setting; no agent seat changes security settings): enable private vulnerability reporting per repository, with the repository's own switch or `PUT /repos/neomjs/<repo>/private-vulnerability-reporting`, which changes nothing else.
   **Not through a security configuration (corrected on 2026-11-15, 22:45Z).** I had pointed the operator to one. A configuration carries code scanning and Dependabot settings along: applied that evening, it failed on 15 repositories (4 with their own code scanning setup, 11 private ones without Advanced Security), left private reporting off everywhere, and switched on CodeQL default setup in 36 repositories and Dependabot security updates in 13 for the first time. The reverts are the operator's; the lists are in this ticket's comment of that evening.
2. **Mine:** re-run the read above and post it here with its time.

If the setting is not wanted for all repositories, the alternative is one sentence in the engine's policy: a finding anywhere in the organisation is reported through the engine's form and names its repository. This ticket then closes on that pull request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1 (human step, owner: @tobiu): private vulnerability reporting is enabled for the organisation's public repositories, or the alternative above is chosen on this ticket. **Decided on 2026-11-15: the operator chose the setting.** It is not switched on yet (read at 22:03:55Z: `false` for `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-skills` and `create-app`). The switch needs an organisation owner; this seat's token holds `maintain`, not `admin`.
- [x] AC-2 (mine): the read over `gh repo list neomjs --visibility public --no-archived` shows `enabled: true` for every repository and is posted here with its time; on the alternative, the policy sentence is merged. Met on 2026-11-15: 46 of 46 between 23:46:06Z and 23:46:24Z, with the revert of that evening, in comment 6903411326.

## Out of Scope

- A default `SECURITY.md` for the organisation (it needs a public `neomjs/.github` repository) and policy files in single repositories: each is its own decision once reports can be received.
- Private repositories: only collaborators see them.
- A response-time commitment, out of scope in #21004 for the same reason.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-15T22:46:23Z

**The security-configuration route was tried and is the wrong one (2026-11-15, read between 22:40Z and 22:45Z)**

I had pointed the operator to a security configuration under the organisation's Advanced Security settings. He applied one. What I can read from outside:

- **It did not do what this ticket asks:** `private-vulnerability-reporting` still answers `true` for `neo` and `false` for the 45 other public repositories (22:40:59Z).
- **It failed on 15 repositories:** 4 public ones that have their own code scanning setup, and 11 private ones, because the organisation has no Advanced Security licence.
- **Where it applied, it switched on more than was asked.** Read from each repository's workflow runs since 22:30Z:
  - CodeQL default setup, for the first time (no earlier run of it in the last 40 runs), in 36 public repositories.
  - Dependabot security updates, for the first time (no Dependabot pull request before), in 13 repositories, 7 of them public; 9 Dependabot pull requests were open by 22:43Z.

The 36 with a new CodeQL default setup:

```
github-content-sync pages benchmarks create-app jsdoc-x liquid-glass-demo pages2 workspace
offscreen-canvas earthquakes krausest chartjs-demo old-website multiwindowcolors
multipleWindow3dScene jsdoc cypress-ct-neo.mjs learning-section neomjs-realworld-example-app
admin-workspace workshops templates shared-offscreen intro2webdev-neo websocket
```

The 7 public ones with new Dependabot security updates: `benchmarks jsdoc-x multipleWindow3dScene jsdoc cypress-ct-neo.mjs workshops js-framework-benchmark`.

What I cannot read with this seat's token: the configuration itself, each repository's security settings, and whether the four repositories with a code scanning conflict took the configuration's other settings.

The body's Fix now names the per-repository switch, which changes nothing else. The reverts need an organisation owner.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-15T23:47:24Z

**Done: the earlier state is back, and private reporting is on in all 46 public repositories (2026-11-15, 23:43Z to 23:46Z)**

- **Source of the earlier state:** the organisation's audit log of that evening. The configuration ran from 22:37:59Z to 22:38:15Z, and every `.enable` event it caused became one row of the revert: CodeQL default setup 41, Dependabot security updates 44, Dependabot alerts 32, secret scanning 45, push protection 45. `neo` has no such event.
- **The revert:** run by the operator under an owner's login, one call per row, each row read again after its write: 252 rows, none failed (49 were already back from two earlier runs).
- **The check:** a state read at 23:43:39Z compared with the earlier state derived from the log shows no difference. No configuration is attached to any repository and none is a default.
- **This ticket's goal, in the same run:** `PUT /repos/neomjs/<repo>/private-vulnerability-reporting` on the 45 other public repositories, which changes nothing else. AC-2, read with a token that is not an owner's between 23:46:06Z and 23:46:24Z: `enabled: true` for 46 of 46.
- **What stays as it is, on purpose:** a public repository created later has the switch off until someone sets it. There is no organisation default after this evening.
- **Not undone through the API, both passive:** the dependency graph on private repositories, which GitHub documents as switched off together with the alerts, and the list of repositories Dependabot may read.
